title: Boston matrix: Zaytoon Foods
subject: Business
source: Written for business/y11 lesson 44 (Pupil PDF worksheet: own exam-style questions, case data and mark-scheme points (teacher-written))
intro: Lesson 44. Place each product, then justify where to invest. All businesses, people and figures in these cases are fictional, made up for practice.

passage.title: Zaytoon Foods
paras: Zaytoon Foods sells Middle Eastern foods to UK supermarkets. It has £150,000 to invest next year.

questions.q: Place each product in the Boston matrix.
questions.a: Olive oil: cash cow (high share, low growth). Za'atar crackers: star (high share, high growth). Hummus dip: question mark (low share, high growth). Pickled turnips: dog (low share, falling market). Stuffed vine leaves: dog (low share, low growth).

questions.q: Justify which product Zaytoon Foods should invest the £150,000 in.
questions.a: Level-marked (9): e.g. the hummus dip (question mark in a 15% growth market could become a star, funded by olive oil's cash) or the crackers (protect a star); compare with the other option; dogs not chosen.

frame.label: Overall, why my choice is better for THIS business

markScheme.a: Level 3 (7-9): a justified choice using the data, developed chains of reasoning, and a comparison showing why it beats the other option. Level 2 (4-6): reasons in context, little comparison. Level 1 (1-3): generic points.
